solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Why lips user curls about love, sotto voce?

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so the letters sit round the next item

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: things that curl twist out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a person curls their lips while murmuring softly about love.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for love goes in among the other eleven letters before they are rearranged into WHISPEROUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotto voce is Italian for 'under the voice', i.e. in a low murmur, and whisperously is an adverb for speaking in a whisper.

clue.text: One's prepared for flood and put in substantive mound

indicators.note: something put in is placed inside another item, so these letters go into the next part

parts.note: sb is the dictionary abbreviation for substantive, i.e. noun
taken as written
an agger is a Roman earthwork or mound

explanation.surface: A person ready for rising water piles up a solid bank of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: AND goes between the S and B of SB, then AGGER follows: S(AND)B + AGGER. 'Substantive' looks like an adjective for the mound but is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbagger is someone who lays sandbags, the usual barrier used to hold back rising floodwater.

clue.text: One monkey or another grabbed by a third

indicators.note: whatever is grabbed is held in the grip of something else, so these letters end up enclosed

parts.note: a sai is a South American capuchin monkey
an imp is a little monkey in the sense of a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A zoo scene: one monkey, or a second one, gets seized by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: Every 'monkey' here is a different word, and 'imp' is a monkey only in the sense of a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: The simpai is a black-crested langur of Sumatra, a species of leaf monkey.

clue.text: Morning place with limitless beer? I may be legless

parts.note: a.m. stands for morning
to place is to put

indicators.note: without limits means without its two ends, so only the inner letters stay

parts.note: the inside of the word beer

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts that endless morning beer could leave them legless, i.e. drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, which suits the beer, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amputee has had a limb removed, so one may literally have no legs.

clue.text: What sounds like buck in pain

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word spoken the same as the following one, not spelt the same

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A riddle about something suffering, like a hurt male deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' suggests a deer but is US slang for a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolour is a literary word for grief or sorrow, a kind of mental suffering.

clue.text: Old-style lucky dip offering one penny cheese wraps

indicators.note: a thing that wraps goes all round something else, holding it inside

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
an, the indefinite article, means one
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A traditional lucky dip offers a penny and cheese parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like a noun, cheese parcels, but it is the verb: the cheese wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bran pie was a tub of bran with small gifts buried in it, dug out at fairs and parties: an old lucky dip.

clue.text: Crawl: good swimming over length

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: letters swimming about drift out of place and settle in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A swimming coach's note: front crawl, good, over a length of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawl' looks like the swimming stroke, matching the pool scene, but it means abase oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel is to crawl in the humbling sense: to fawn or behave obsequiously, even physically on hands and knees.

clue.text: Holiday let supplying indescribable quality in borders of Gironde

indicators.note: one item sits in the other, so its letters are placed inside
the borders of a word are its outer edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: first and last letters of Gironde
'it' is that indefinable something, especially sex appeal

explanation.surface: A French rental cottage in the Gironde region has a charm beyond words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as a noun is that indefinable allure, as in an 'It girl'; the Gironde is a region of south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: A gîte is a furnished holiday home in France, rented out to visitors.

clue.text: Bull heading for cows, gripped by rising surge

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards
something gripped is held inside, so this letter goes in the middle

parts.note: a surge of water is a tide

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of cows

explanation.surface: A farmyard: a bull charges at the cows amid a rising flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' and 'cows' form a herd, but this bull is the Pope's.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal bull is a formal decree issued by the Pope, so it is an edict.

clue.text: Nude photo maybe exciting ardent creeps (12, two words)

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racy picture gets keen, unsavoury men worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre spread is the middle double page of a magazine, notoriously where pin-up nudes appeared; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Bit of a hunk, I'm tedious — ring off

definitions.text: Bit of a hunk, I'm tedious — ring off

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the named letters are dropped from the word
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of hunk
taken as written
tedious means boring
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A handsome man admits he is dull and tells the caller to hang up.
explanation.walkthrough: BORING without RING leaves BO. The whole clue is also the himbo speaking: a bit of a hunk who bores.
explanation.definitionFit: A himbo is a good-looking but vacuous man, so a hunk who confesses to dullness fits the word.

clue.text: Strong ledge? Most kitchens'll have one

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
a ridge is a narrow raised ledge

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a sturdy shelf as standard kitchen kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong ledge' reads like a shelf, but f is forte, a music abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is standard equipment, found in nearly every domestic kitchen.

clue.text: Angler's third dab, a late one

indicators.note: a word's third means its third letter, counted from the start

parts.note: third letter of angler
a dab or dab hand is an expert, also called a oner

explanation.surface: A fisherman's flatfish, caught dead or caught late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dab' looks like the flatfish an angler lands; it means an expert, and a oner is British slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone dead or doomed, so 'a late one' means one who has died.

clue.text: Myself and friend mum's enveloped in fantastic jumper

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are shaped into something odd

parts.note: I refers to myself
a pal is a friend
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: Me, my friend and Mum all wrapped in an amazing knitted pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater, which suits being 'enveloped', but it is an animal that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope famous for its huge bounding leaps, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: What's your poison? First off, spoon it out

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is taken away
out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: spoon with its first letter taken off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman asks for your drink order, then spoons it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's your poison?' is a jokey way of asking what someone will drink; a potion is the drink that answers it.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a dose of liquid, often magical or medicinal, and poison itself is one kind.

clue.text: Gelato? Sam's turned up for one, numero uno

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards
'X for Y' means X stands in place of Y, swapping one letter group for another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be turned round
a means one, the letter to replace
numero uno is Italian for number one

explanation.surface: At the ice-cream parlour, Sam shows up to buy one for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sam's' as 'Sam has': SAM has PU in place of A, giving SPUM, then ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spumone is a moulded Italian ice cream, so it is a type of gelato, the Italian word for ice cream.

clue.text: Nut paste, savvy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pâté, a spread, such as a nut pâté
second meaning: ..., the head, and hence brains or wits

explanation.walkthrough: One spelling covers both the savoury spread and the old word for the head, read here as intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a smooth savoury spread, which nut pâté is; pate is the crown of the head, standing for brains or nous.

clue.text: Folder made of PVC fabric, not hard inside

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is left out
inside says the letter dropped comes from the middle of the word, not an end

parts.note: pleather is plastic imitation leather
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A document folder is made from vinyl material with a soft interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folder' suggests a stationery file, but it means a person or machine that folds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleater makes pleats, the folds in fabric, so it is literally one that folds.

clue.text: Part of terrible ordeal once? One could get frailer with it

indicators.note: the answer could become another word, meaning its letters, reshuffled with an addition, form a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trial by fire was a cruel ordeal that would make anyone weaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters together with IT rearrange to FRAILER plus IT, i.e. remove IT from the answer and the rest is FRAILER reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial fire, the fire used in trial by ordeal, was one form of the medieval ordeal of guilt.

clue.text: Old furnace routine coming up, hot one to be stoked

indicators.note: a furnace is stoked by putting fuel into it, so these letters go inside
in a down clue coming up means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a rota is a routine schedule of duties
h is the abbreviation for hot
an means one

explanation.surface: An old furnace's daily routine, with fuel fed in to keep one burning hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoked' fits the furnace scene and also tells you to feed letters into the reversed routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An athanor was the self-feeding furnace used by alchemists, kept at constant heat.

clue.text: Bit of Jack Frost's art? Top one could be perfection (7, two words)

indicators.note: the answer with an added word could be another word, so their letters together are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: the result of the shuffle

explanation.surface: Frost patterns on a window are a masterpiece, the best of them perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus TOP rearranges to PERFECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice fern is a fern-like frost pattern on glass, the sort of design attributed to Jack Frost, personification of frost.

clue.text: River edge circling round damaged tree — this gauges current

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: a hem is an edge of cloth
O is round in shape

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so its letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A riverbank scene of a damaged tree, with a measure of how strong the flow is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests the river's flow, but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheometer is an instrument for measuring electric current, from Greek rheos, a stream.

clue.text: Perennial landlord, absent

parts.note: a landlord of an inn acts as host
a is the abbreviation for absent

explanation.surface: A pub landlord who is perpetually away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' reads as an adjective for the absent landlord; it is a noun, a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a leafy garden plant that returns every year, so it is a perennial.

clue.text: Major industry like pottery, core doubled

indicators.note: doubling a part means a second copy of it is set in next to the first

parts.note: Ming is the Chinese dynasty famous for porcelain, describing a style of pottery
the core of that pottery word, its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A big industry, like ceramics, which centres on doubling its output.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of MING is IN; doubling it gives M + IN + IN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining, extracting coal and ore from the ground, was a staple heavy industry.

clue.text: Those devoted to Charles as involved with line

indicators.note: letters involved with each other get tangled up, emerging in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Followers of King Charles fall into line behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charles is Charles Lamb, who wrote the Essays of Elia, not a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Elians are admirers of Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia.

clue.text: Celestial phenomenon I had seen after Christmas looking up

indicators.note: seen after something means placed behind it, so this piece comes second
in a down clue looking up means reading upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Gazing skyward after Christmas, someone spots something in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen after' places I'D after the reversed Christmas word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leonid is a meteor from the November shower appearing to come from the constellation Leo.

clue.text: Love of this corrupted? Possibly

indicators.note: something corrupted is spoilt from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero, the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral question: did love of something lead a person astray?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue alludes to 'the love of money is the root of all evil': love of ooftish may well corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooftish is old slang, from Yiddish, for money, the thing whose love proverbially corrupts.

clue.text: A portion of half rations for mendicant monks

indicators.note: a portion is a piece cut from the whole, so the letters run inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Begging friars live on meagre food, half the normal rations.
explanation.definitionFit: Frati is Italian for brothers, friars of the mendicant orders who lived by begging.

clue.text: Move to one side parking military vehicle

parts.note: jee, or gee, is a call to a horse to turn aside
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: An order to shift over and park an army truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The jeep is a small rugged four-wheel-drive vehicle first built for the US Army.

clue.text: Unending carousal, past ceasing

indicators.note: without an ending means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a blind is a drinking bout, a binge

explanation.surface: An endless drinking spree finally stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past' marks the definition as obsolete; BLIND loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blin is an obsolete word for stopping, a cessation, so it is an old term for ceasing.

clue.text: Organized a do — if included in price … it must be (7, two words)

definitions.text: Organized a do — if included in price … it must be

indicators.note: something included in another sits inside it

parts.note: pr is an abbreviation for price

indicators.note: organized means arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An event organiser notes that if a party is in the price, it has to be funded.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: anything included in a price must be paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something included in a price has been settled with money, so the do is covered financially.

clue.text: Part of pedestal inscribed for despot

indicators.note: part of the phrase means a stretch of its letters, running inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A tyrant's name is carved on a statue's base.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator, the model of a tyrant.

clue.text: Language group from former protectorate in north-east

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits between its letters

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east
Aden was a British protectorate in southern Arabia

explanation.surface: Languages spread from an old colonial territory in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: Aden, now part of Yemen, was a British protectorate until 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: Na-Dene is a family of North American native languages, including Navajo and Apache.

clue.text: Member of large US minority group making money in SE Asian country

definitions.text: Member of large US minority group

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: Lao is the short official name of Laos
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A US immigrant earns a living in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' belongs to the definition, not an L; Laos is called Lao in its official name, and tin is old slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latino is a person of Latin American descent in the US, one of the country's largest minorities.

clue.text: A metal that turns irrigation device

indicators.note: something that turns round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
iron is a metal

explanation.surface: A metal wheel that rotates to water the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' suits the wheel in the picture but also reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A noria is a water wheel with buckets that lifts water into irrigation channels.

clue.text: Fringe, funny and direct — it's out on a limb

indicators.note: funny means strange or odd, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
to direct something somewhere is to send it

explanation.surface: Fringe theatre, comic and blunt, takes a risk out on a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out on a limb' sounds like the idiom for being exposed, but it is literal: at the extremity of an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The fingertip sits at the very end of the arm, i.e. at the outermost point of a limb.
